categorias_que.rastreador: A public list recognises it as tracking: it is used to follow you from one site to the next.
categorias_que.publicidad: It is on the advertising lists: it shows you ads, or measures them.
categorias_que.telemetria: Usage data a program sends back to its maker.
categorias_que.esperado: What a computer needs to work: system updates, certificates, the system’s own security and connectivity checks, time, recognised messaging and video calls, and what GUARDIANA needs for its licence.
categorias_que.desconocido: No open tracking list knows it. It does not mean it is suspicious.
categorias_que.red_local: Devices in your home finding each other. It does not go out to the internet.
categorias_que.entrega: A network that carries other companies’ content. Not the destination: the road.
categorias_que.de_empresa: Its owner is known (the next column names the company) and no list marks it as tracking or advertising, but the name does not say what it is for. A label, never a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_anuncios: No list has it yet, but the name carries a technical term from ad auctions (prebid, rtb, ssp, dsp, cookie syncing). The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_pago: A payment or a subscription at that company: the name carries “checkout”, “pay”, “billing” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_cuenta: Signing in or your account data at that company: the name carries “login”, “accounts”, “auth” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_medicion: Counts what you do in its app or site, for the company itself: the name carries “analytics”, “metrics”, “events”, “pixel” or similar. No public list marks it as tracking; the name says so.
categorias_que.pista_notificaciones: The notifications that reach your device: the name carries “push”, “notifications” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_actualizaciones: Downloading updates or the installer: the name carries “update”, “download”, “release” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_seguridad: Security checks of the browser or the system: the name carries “safebrowsing”, “smartscreen”, “captcha” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_correo: Your email: the name carries “mail”, “smtp” or “imap”. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_mensajes: Chat or messaging of that company: the name carries “chat”, “messages” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_sincronizacion: Syncs or keeps a copy in the cloud: the name carries “drive” or “backup”. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_contenido: Images, video, files or fonts the page needs to display: the name carries “cdn”, “static”, “img”, “media” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_configuracion: The program asks for its settings or checks options: the name carries “config”, “settings”, “flags” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_app: The program or app talking to its own company’s server in order to work: the name carries “api”, “gateway”, “backend” or similar. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.pista_web: That company’s site or app, the one you opened: the name is its domain or starts with “www”. The name says so; it is not a verdict.
categorias_que.sector: A {sector} website: what it does, from our open list of sectors. It says what it is, not whether to trust it.

cli.dns.deshacer_pendiente: The change failed half-way and could not be fully undone. The copy of your previous setting is still saved: run guardiana dns --restore to put it back.
cli.observe.no_comparte: Queries from {dispositivo} are recorded but not shown here: its owner does not share the detail with the home panel.
cli.observe.vuelve_licencia: The licence is valid again: GUARDIANA is this computer’s DNS again and is watching.
cli.observe.vuelve_licencia_sin_dns: The licence is valid again: GUARDIANA is watching again.
cli.observe.vuelve_hogar: Home Mode is on again, as you had it.
cli.observe.relevo: Home Mode: the router still sends the home’s queries here. While GUARDIANA stands aside it only passes them on to {upstream} from {addr}, without looking at them or writing them down, so nobody is left without internet. Put the router’s DNS back as it was (or to automatic) when you can.
cli.observe.relevo_sin_arriba: Home Mode: I cannot find where to pass the home’s queries on, so I cannot relay them. If the router still sends the home’s queries here, put its DNS back as it was (or to automatic) now: without that, the phones and the rest are left without internet.
cli.observe.relevo_error: Home Mode: I cannot listen on the network to pass the home’s queries on ({error}). If the router still sends the home’s queries here, put its DNS back as it was (or to automatic) now.
cli.observe.upstream_propio: The DNS the network hands out is this very computer (the router gives out its address, as Home Mode asks), and GUARDIANA cannot ask itself: it asks {servers}.
cli.observe.solo_propio: The only DNS this computer knows is itself (the router gives out its address, as Home Mode asks), and GUARDIANA cannot ask itself. Set a fixed DNS on this computer (the router’s or your provider’s) or give one with --upstream IP.

cli.uso:
Usage:
  guardiana observe [--listen IP:PORT] [--upstream IP[:PORT]]... [--db PATH] [--canary] [--open] [--no-panel] [--panel-listen IP:PORT]
  guardiana ledger [--check | --wipe | --self | --last N] [--db PATH]
  guardiana export [--csv | --json] [--out FILE] [--device ID] [--category C] [--signal S] [--verdict V] [--limit N] [--db PATH]
  guardiana dns [--status | --apply --yes | --restore] [--db PATH]
  guardiana licencia [clave KEY | comprobar]
  guardiana trampa [crear | lista | quitar ID]   (trap files: a name that only exists inside)
  guardiana apps [--seconds N] [--crudo]   (Windows: which program asks for each name, watch only)
  guardiana verify [--json]
  guardiana reglas [deshacer ID | deshacer-hoy]
  guardiana informe               (weekly home report)
  guardiana hogar [status | on | off]
  guardiana service [install | uninstall | start | stop | status]
  guardiana panel                (opens the panel in the browser)
  guardiana menu [--choice N]     (interactive test menu)
  guardiana version

Download {archivo} from the install page, open a terminal in that folder and type “guardiana verify”: it checks the signature on your computer, without connecting to anything.

cli.verify.firma.ok: Signature: correct. The program is signed with the GUARDIANA key it carries inside: {clave}. Compare it with the one published at guardianagroup.com/en/install.html.
cli.verify.firma.mal: Signature: does NOT match. The program or its signature has changed. Do not use it until this is cleared up.
cli.verify.registro.sin_archivo: Public record: there is no ledger.jsonl in this folder or next to the program. Download it from the install page into the same folder and run verify from there: it looks this hash up in the public record, on your computer.
cli.verify.registro.no_esta: Public record: this hash is NOT in ledger.jsonl. If this is a released version, something is off.
cli.verify.registro.ok: Public record: matches version {v} published on {fecha} (Rekor {rekor}).
cli.verify.dns.guardiana_primario: GUARDIANA changed the DNS: this computer’s queries go through it.
cli.verify.dns.guardiana_no_primario: GUARDIANA changed the DNS but RIGHT NOW the queries do not go through it: the system changed it back. The service reapplies it every minute; if it persists, use guardiana dns --apply --yes.
cli.verify.dns.guardiana_desconocido: GUARDIANA changed the DNS; could not check whether the queries go through it right now.
cli.verify.dns.sin_cambiar: GUARDIANA has not changed the system DNS.
cli.extracto.otra_clave: This ledger does not belong to this version of GUARDIANA: it was created by a version signed with a different key, and, for safety, the two are never mixed. If you are coming from a test version, move the ledger file elsewhere and GUARDIANA will start a new one. If you were not expecting this, delete nothing and write to hola@guardianagroup.com.
cli.verify.dns.solo_guardiana_sin_copia: System DNS: GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1) and nothing else. Every query from this computer goes through it.
cli.verify.dns.solo_guardiana_ajustes: System DNS: only GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1), according to the settings. Whether queries really arrive is what the check below says.
cli.verify.dns.apunta_sin_copia: This computer points at GUARDIANA, but GUARDIANA did not make that change: it has no record of the DNS you had before. On uninstall it will not be able to put it back exactly as it was. Apply it again from the panel so it is recorded.
cli.verify.vigilante: Guard Mode on for: {aparatos}. On those devices everything outside the declared scope is blocked, not only what the agent asks for.
cli.verify.hogar.aparcado: Home Mode: set aside, because the trial or the subscription ended. While GUARDIANA stands aside, port 53 stays open on the local network: it passes the home’s queries on, without looking at them or writing them down, so nobody is left without internet until you put the router’s DNS back.

cli.verify.puertos.aviso: WARNING: Home Mode is off and there are GUARDIANA ports open towards the network. Wait a minute and check again; if it stays like this, tell us.
cli.verify.lista: List {id}: {n} entries, shipped inside the program; fetched on {fecha}.
cli.verify.cadena.mal: Ledger: the chain is BROKEN. See guardiana ledger --check.

cli.observe.reconfigurando: Change in the home network or in Home Mode: GUARDIANA reopens its ports without stopping.
cli.observe.sin_arriba: The DNS of your network ({upstream}) has not answered for a minute. GUARDIANA gives this computer its DNS back as it was, so you keep your internet, and will ask again every minute.
cli.observe.vuelve_arriba: The DNS of your network answers again: GUARDIANA is this computer’s DNS once more.
cli.dns.estado.guardiana_primero: This computer’s queries go to GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1).
cli.dns.aplicado_panel: Done. This PC now goes through GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1). It used to resolve with: {originales}. It can be undone in “Status”.
cli.dns.consentimiento_si: To accept, repeat the command with --yes.
cli.dns.reserva_secundario: The resolver you have now stays as the secondary: if GUARDIANA stops, the computer keeps resolving through it.
cli.dns.solo_guardiana: On this computer GUARDIANA becomes the only resolver. That is what stops any query that goes through the system DNS slipping past it: systemd-resolved picks among the servers it has, it does not ask them in order, so leaving the old one as a second would mean part of the queries would never be seen. The service comes back by itself if it stops, and guardiana dns --restore puts everything back exactly as it was.
cli.dns.solo_guardiana_windows: On this computer GUARDIANA becomes the only DNS, over IPv6 too. That way no query that goes through the system DNS slips past it, and Edge does not go off to an encrypted DNS of its own. GUARDIANA keeps asking the servers you had, from the inside. If the service stops, the computer gets its previous DNS back until it starts again, and uninstalling leaves it exactly as it was.
cli.dns.solo_guardiana_mac: On this Mac GUARDIANA becomes the only DNS. That way no query that goes through the system DNS slips past it, and Chrome or Edge do not go off on their own to an encrypted DNS. GUARDIANA keeps asking the network’s servers behind the scenes. If the service stops, the Mac gets its previous DNS back until it starts again, and uninstalling leaves it exactly as it was.
cli.dns.camino_ok: Checked: a query made by Windows just now reached GUARDIANA.
cli.dns.camino_no: WARNING: a query made by Windows just now did NOT reach GUARDIANA, so you will not see anything yet. Disconnect the Wi‑Fi and connect it again (or restart) and check again in “Verify”. If it stays like this, write to hola@guardianagroup.com.
cli.dns.guardiana_no_contesta: Nothing changed: GUARDIANA is not answering on 127.0.0.1, and pointing this computer there would leave it without internet. Start the service (guardiana service start) and run the command again.
cli.dns.camino_no_deshecho: A query made just now by this computer did NOT reach GUARDIANA, so the DNS was put back exactly as it was and nothing changed. Disconnect the Wi‑Fi and connect it again (or restart) and run the command again. If it stays like this, write to hola@guardianagroup.com.
cli.verify.dns.guardiana_con_reserva: System DNS: GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1), with {dns} as the fallback. If GUARDIANA stops, the computer asks the fallback and those queries are not written down.
cli.verify.dns.por_guardiana: System DNS: GUARDIANA (127.0.0.1), which forwards to {dns}.
cli.verify.dns.camino_ok: Real test: a query made by the system just now reached GUARDIANA.
cli.verify.dns.camino_no: Real test: a query made by the system just now did NOT reach GUARDIANA.
cli.observe.caducado: The trial is over and there is no active subscription. GUARDIANA has put this computer’s DNS back exactly as it was and has stopped watching: your internet keeps working the same. Your ledger is whole on your disk and you can take it with you. To watch again, activate your key in the panel.
cli.observe.caducado_plus: The subscription has ended. GUARDIANA has put this computer’s DNS back as it was and has stopped watching: your internet keeps working the same. The ledger is whole on your disk and you can take it. To watch again, activate your key in the panel.
cli.verify.dns.camino_no.parado: The GUARDIANA service is stopped and the settings still point at it, so nothing answers: start the service (guardiana service start) or give back the previous DNS with guardiana dns --restore.
cli.verify.dns.camino_no.sin_servicio: GUARDIANA is not installed as a service and the settings still point at it, so nothing answers: give back the previous DNS with guardiana dns --restore.

panel.hogar_firewall_manual: On this system the firewall rule is added by hand, and only if you have one running: let in, from your local network, ports 53 (udp and tcp), 7443/tcp (the phones’ panel) and 80/tcp (the checker page). With ufw: sudo ufw allow from 192.168.0.0/16 to any port 53 && sudo ufw allow from 192.168.0.0/16 to any port 7443 proto tcp && sudo ufw allow from 192.168.0.0/16 to any port 80 proto tcp (if your network starts with 10., use 10.0.0.0/8 instead of 192.168.0.0/16). With firewalld, in your Wi‑Fi’s zone (see it with “firewall-cmd --get-active-zones”; here, home): sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=home --add-service=dns --add-port=7443/tcp --add-port=80/tcp && sudo firewall-cmd --reload.

panel.reglas_titulo: Rules: what is blocked and what is allowed
panel.reglas_lead: No rule exists unless you create it. Every block records who decided it and when. Undoing never deletes: it records that it was undone.
panel.reglas_inviolables: Broad rules wait and respect the essentials: a whole category, the whole home or Guard Mode block nothing until GUARDIANA has watched for 24 hours, and a category or Guard Mode never touch system updates, certificates, the system’s own security and connectivity checks, time, recognised messaging and video calls, or what GUARDIANA needs for its licence. One name you pick is blocked from the first minute (for the whole home, once that day is over); if it is one of those essentials, or the device has been watched for less than a day, you are asked first.
panel.reglas_nueva_lead: Block or allow an exact name, a family of names (the domain and everything under it) or a whole category, for one device or for the whole home.
panel.reglas_ninguna: There are no rules. GUARDIANA only watches.
panel.leyenda_desconocido: “Local network” is the devices of your home finding each other: it does not go out to the internet. “Delivery” is a network that carries other companies’ content: not the destination, the road. “Its site”, “your account”, “its server”, “content”, “settings”, “measurement”… is what the name itself says (www, login, api, cdn, config, analytics…): a hint, not a check. “Service” is a name of a known company that no list marks and whose name does not say what it is for. “Unclassified” means that no public list knows it, and neither does our company list; not that it is suspicious. “Sport”, “news”, “banking”… is what a well-known website does, from our open list of sectors.
panel.leyenda_colores: The three colours of the category. Green: normal, what a service needs to work (its website, its server, your account, updates, content, your home network). Orange: worth a look; it measures what you do, serves ads or nobody knows it (advertising, telemetry, measurement, ads, unclassified). Red: alert; a public list recognises it as tracking, the company is registered as a data broker, or it tries to evade monitoring. It is a way of reading the category, not a verdict: click the label to learn what it means, and block or unblock each row with its button.

panel.borrado_lead: In almost every country with a data protection law, companies that keep your personal data have to delete it when you ask. This page helps you ask, with a letter ready to send that cites the law where you live.
panel.borrado_aviso_abogados: We are not lawyers: this is a template based on the law it cites.
panel.borrado_privado: Your name and email are only used to fill in the letters on this page. They are not saved in the extract or in any GUARDIANA record, and GUARDIANA sends them to no one: you send the letter, from your own email. If you tick “Remember them in this browser”, they are kept only in this browser, on this computer.

panel.borrado_sin_derecho_limitado: Here the law gives no general right to have your data deleted. The letter asks for what it does give you: to know what they hold, to correct it, to withdraw your consent, and to have them destroy what they no longer need.
panel.borrado_sin_derecho_ninguno: Here no general law makes a company delete your data. The letter is a request, not a legal demand, and it says so.

My name is {nombre} and I am writing to exercise my right of access under {articulo} ({ley}).

Please tell me:
1. Whether you process personal data about me and, if so, which, in a copy I can read.
2. Where you obtained it, what you use it for and on what legal basis.
3. Whom you have shared or sold it to, in particular advertising companies or data brokers.
4. How long you keep it, and whether you make automated decisions or profiles about me with it.

Please answer within the period the law sets: {plazo}.

You can reply to this email: {correo}. If you need any further detail to find me in your systems, tell me; I am not sending more than necessary.
{evidencia}
{fecha}

{nombre}

This screen shows which internet addresses it contacts and what its own maker says about each one. Someone independent and open source has to watch the watcher.
panel.av_limite: What GUARDIANA can see: the name of every address the antivirus processes ask for on this computer. What it cannot see: the content of what it sends; anything sent without asking Windows for those names (through its own resolver or to a fixed address), or anything downloaded through other Windows programs such as Windows Update.

panel.av_historial_limite: We only include decisions by public authorities with a published official source. We leave out lawsuits between private parties, settlements without a decision and press reports. If a decision was appealed or partly annulled, we say so.

panel.av_tema_marketing: What else it uses it for
panel.av_como_1: Windows reports which program asked for each address and who signs that program. GUARDIANA recognises each antivirus’s processes by their file name, using a public list we maintain (antivirus.txt).
panel.av_como_2: Next to each address we show what it is for according to the maker’s own documentation, with the link. If the maker does not document it, we say so without accusing anyone: it may be a legitimate service they have not published. You have the right to ask them.
panel.av_como_3: If you want to know what data your antivirus company holds about you, «Make them erase you» prepares the letter to request it or to ask for its erasure.
panel.av_nunca: GUARDIANA will never ask you to turn off your antivirus. Watching it does not mean removing it: it is still a protection you need.
panel.av_sancion_ftc_avast: According to the FTC, Avast collected the browsing history of users of its antivirus and extensions, kept it indefinitely and sold it to more than 100 companies through its subsidiary Jumpshot, while claiming to protect their privacy. The order bans it from selling or licensing browsing data for advertising and requires it to delete the data passed to Jumpshot, notify those affected and pay $16.5 million to compensate consumers.
panel.av_sancion_ftc_avg: The FTC order against Avast includes AVG products (same group) among those covered by the duty to notify users. It is not a second penalty: same case, same payment.
panel.av_sancion_uoou_avast: The Czech data protection authority fined Avast Software for processing personal data without a legal basis: it passed its users’ browsing data to its subsidiary Jumpshot, data that allowed at least some of them to be identified, and did not inform them properly. In 2025 a court upheld the breaches but annulled the amount (see the ruling).
panel.av_sancion_msp_avast: The Prague Municipal Court confirmed that Avast committed both breaches, but annulled the figure of about 100 million affected users and the confirmation of the amount, and sent the case back to the authority to recalculate it. Until then, the 351 million korunas are not a final amount.
panel.av_sancion_cma_norton: The UK competition and consumer authority investigated automatic subscription renewals. Norton undertook to let customers cancel with a pro-rata refund after renewal, to state the renewal price up front and not to present the first price as a discount. There was no fine and no admission of wrongdoing.
panel.av_sancion_cma_mcafee: The UK competition and consumer authority investigated automatic subscription renewals. McAfee undertook to let customers cancel with a pro-rata refund after renewal, to simplify refunds and to state the renewal price up front. There was no fine and no admission of wrongdoing.
panel.av_sancion_bis_kaspersky: The US Department of Commerce banned Kaspersky from selling its antivirus in the country and, from 29 September 2024, from updating it, on national-security grounds. It is not a fine, and people who keep using it commit no offence.
panel.av_sancion_canada_kaspersky: The Government of Canada blocked and removed Kaspersky applications from official mobile phones. It only covers government devices.
panel.av_sancion_bsi_kaspersky: Germany’s Federal Office for Information Security officially warned against using Kaspersky’s antivirus and recommended replacing it. It is neither a fine nor a ban. A German administrative court rejected Kaspersky’s urgent application to withdraw the warning.
panel.av_sancion_dhs_kaspersky: The US Department of Homeland Security ordered federal government agencies to identify and remove Kaspersky products from their systems. It only covers the federal government.

panel.av_mercado_lead: Many people do not know how much money the antivirus business moves or where it comes from. These figures are from official or recognised sources; each has its link.
panel.av_mercado_1: That is the size Gartner forecasts for the worldwide consumer security market in 2028, growing about 4 % a year.
panel.av_mercado_2: Gen Digital —owner of Norton, Avast, AVG and Avira— earned this in its fiscal year 2025, with 40.4 million paying customers. One company holds four of the best-known antivirus brands.
panel.av_mercado_3: Kaspersky earned this in 2024, its all-time record, despite being banned on US government computers.
panel.av_mercado_4: companies to which, according to the FTC, Avast sold through its Jumpshot subsidiary the browsing history it collected with its antivirus and its browser extensions. In June 2024, an FTC order agreed with Avast banned it from selling or licensing browsing data for advertising and made it pay $16.5 million.
panel.av_mercado_5: Microsoft Defender comes free inside Windows 10 and 11, so it is on almost every Windows computer in the world and is the most-used antivirus. The exact split against paid ones is not reliably published.
panel.av_mercado_6: In 2021, after investigating subscriptions that renew by themselves, the UK competition and consumer authority accepted undertakings from Norton and McAfee to ease cancellation and refund the pro-rata part to those who did not want to renew. There was no fine.
panel.av_mercado_limite: The figures change every year and companies report in different currencies and calendars; take them as the order of magnitude of the business, not as today’s exact number.
